nodes.label: Quality & Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Layered test strategy: the everyday build stays fast and hermetic, deeper heavier checks are opt-in so they never slow down day-to-day development.

nodes.label: Two-tier Default Build (Unit + Integration)
nodes.rationale: Unit tests (*Test.java, Surefire, pure Mockito/JUnit) and integration tests (*IT.java, Failsafe, @SpringBootTest on real H2). mvn clean verify runs both tiers with no Docker required, keeping the required CI gate cheap and hermetic.

nodes.label: failover.store.async=false in Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: Integration tests run with failover.store.async=false so writes are synchronous and assertions are deterministic; async writes would race the assertion.

nodes.label: Opt-in Deep Checks (Phase 3 Hardening T-1..T-4)
nodes.rationale: Added in the Phase 3 hardening pass from audit findings T-1 to T-4. Each heavy check is gated behind a Maven profile so the default build is unaffected; in CI dialect-its and mutation run as advisory non-blocking checks while the H2 build remains the required gate.

nodes.label: Concurrency Tests (T-2)
nodes.rationale: Contention coverage for multi-tenant store routing and the async executor path; part of the default build.

nodes.label: Architecture Tests / ArchUnit (T-3)
nodes.rationale: ArchUnit rules enforce the store-decorator invariants the compiler cannot express; part of the default build.

nodes.label: Dialect Integration Tests (T-1, ADR 43)
nodes.rationale: Audit finding T-1 / ADR 43. Non-H2 merge SQL was previously verified by string assertion only, so a grammar typo would fail no test; at runtime the first failing store() throws BadSqlGrammarException, the store permanently flips to the INSERT/UPDATE fallback and the broken merge is silently masked. Real containers close that gap.

nodes.label: Native Merge/Upsert Dialect
nodes.rationale: Per-database atomic upsert: H2 MERGE INTO ... KEY, PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, MySQL/MariaDB INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, Oracle MERGE INTO ... USING SELECT FROM DUAL, other databases fall back to INSERT + UPDATE.

nodes.label: DefaultFailoverStoreQueryResolver
nodes.rationale: Selects the merge dialect per database (ADR 13: JDBC native merge/upsert dialect detection and runtime fallback). Adding a dialect means adding the SQL constant plus a contains() branch here.

nodes.label: AbstractDialectIT
nodes.rationale: Holds the shared store/merge/find/cleanByExpiry/delete round-trip scenario so a new dialect only supplies a @Container and DDL subclass, with no test logic rewritten.

nodes.label: dialect-its Maven Profile
nodes.rationale: *DialectIT is excluded from the default failsafe config and runs only under the dialect-its profile, which needs a Docker daemon. Testcontainers JARs stay test-scoped so the sources always compile; only container startup is gated.

nodes.label: Oracle Intentionally Not Containerised
nodes.rationale: The gvenzl/oracle-free image is ~2 GB with slow startup and licensing caveats; Oracle MERGE USING DUAL stays string-asserted because PostgreSQL + MySQL + MariaDB already cover the two distinct non-H2 merge grammars.

nodes.label: String-assertion-only Verification Gap
nodes.rationale: Asserting on the SQL string proves the constant exists, not that the grammar is valid; the defect only surfaces at runtime and is then masked by the silent fallback.

nodes.label: Mutation Testing (T-4, ADR 46)
nodes.rationale: Audit finding T-4 / ADR 46. Line coverage proves a line executed, not that an assertion would catch a bug; expiry-boundary logic (isExpired, cleanByExpiry, < vs <=) and key derivation are exactly where off-by-one changes pass every existing test.

nodes.label: PIT (pitest)
nodes.rationale: Mutates bytecode (flipping conditionals, changing boundaries, replacing return values) and reruns the tests. Requires pitest-maven >= 1.20 and pitest-junit5-plugin >= 1.2.3 on JUnit Platform 6, otherwise the coverage minion exits with UNKNOWN_ERROR; the surefire argLine carrying the JaCoCo agent is deliberately not inherited by the PIT minion.

nodes.label: Surviving Mutant
nodes.rationale: A bytecode change no test noticed — evidence of weak assertions rather than missing execution.

nodes.label: mutation Maven Profile
nodes.rationale: PIT is scoped to failover-core only: the parent POM defaults pitest.skip=true and failover-core overrides it to false, so a reactor -am build does not run PIT on dependency modules with no target classes (which would fail with 'No mutations found' under failWhenNoMutations=true).

nodes.label: 95% Mutation Coverage Gate
nodes.rationale: Mandated and blocking in CI: the build fails below 95% across all of com.societegenerale.failover.core. failWhenNoMutations=true ensures a zero-mutation misconfiguration fails loudly so the gate can never pass vacuously. Current score: 216 mutations, 208 killed (96%), test strength 99%.

nodes.label: Equivalent / Unkillable Mutants
nodes.rationale: Remaining survivors cannot be killed without changing production code: unreachable catch (NoSuchMethodException) in overridesToString, dead areturn after sneakyThrow in RethrowIfNoRecoveryMethodExceptionPolicy, a setMetadata on an already-mutated instance, a null-envelope return on the not-found recover path, and four negate-conditional mutants on the metric publish(...) call duplicated by finally-block inlining.

nodes.label: Assertion Strengthening to Reach the Gate
nodes.rationale: Required asserting returned values rather than delegate invocation, pinning castToStringValue warn-vs-no-warn branching with log capture, a positive ReferentialPayload.toString assertion, exercising populateAdditionalInfoOnMetadata, and bounding the reported duration-ns so a subtraction-to-addition mutant is caught.
nodes.norm_label: assertion strengthening to reach the gate

nodes.label: @Failover Annotation
nodes.rationale: Method-level, RUNTIME-retained, documented annotation placed on any Spring-managed bean method to declare failover behaviour.

nodes.label: name attribute
nodes.rationale: Required unique identifier used as FAILOVER_NAME in the store unless domain is set; must be unique across the application, and appears in logs and the startup scanner report.

nodes.label: expiryDuration attribute
nodes.rationale: Numeric part of the TTL (default 1), ignored when expiryDurationExpression is non-empty.

nodes.label: expiryUnit attribute
nodes.rationale: ChronoUnit part of the TTL (default HOURS), ignored when expiryUnitExpression is non-empty.

nodes.label: expiryDurationExpression attribute
nodes.rationale: Spring property placeholder or SpEL evaluating to a long; externalises the TTL per environment instead of hard-coding it in the annotation, and takes precedence over expiryDuration.

nodes.label: expiryUnitExpression attribute
nodes.rationale: Spring property placeholder or SpEL evaluating to a ChronoUnit name string; overrides expiryUnit when non-empty.

nodes.label: keyGenerator attribute
nodes.rationale: Bean name of a custom KeyGenerator, used to override key derivation for complex or order-sensitive arguments; DefaultKeyGenerator applies when empty.

nodes.label: expiryPolicy attribute
nodes.rationale: Bean name of a custom ExpiryPolicy to override TTL computation; DefaultExpiryPolicy applies when empty.

nodes.label: payloadSplitter attribute
nodes.rationale: Bean name of a PayloadSplitter; when set it enables scatter/gather mode, otherwise standard single-key behaviour applies.

nodes.label: recoverAll attribute
nodes.rationale: Forces the scatter recover-all path even when args are non-empty, for findAll-style methods whose args are filters (status, region) not entity identities. Without it scatter would split filter args into per-slice keys that all miss, since entries were stored by entity ID. Empty args already trigger recover-all automatically. Warning: recoverAll=true with a splitter whose splitOnRecover reads args throws IndexOutOfBoundsException or produces wrong slices, so use a separate recover-all splitter bean.

nodes.label: domain attribute
nodes.rationale: Optional logical namespace: when set, both key hashing and FAILOVER_NAME use domain instead of name, so multiple @Failover annotations for the same business entity share store entries (a scatter store populated by findByCodes is readable by findByCode). All annotations sharing a domain should use the same TTL; mismatches are warned at startup and last writer wins.

nodes.label: Two-splitter Pattern for recoverAll
nodes.rationale: Use a separate PayloadSplitter bean for the recover-all path whose splitOnRecover returns a single placeholder context ignoring or preserving filter args, and whose delegateR.recoverAll() fetches all slices by name.

nodes.label: Reference Section
nodes.rationale: Complete API reference for public annotation attributes, SPI interfaces, and generated Javadoc; concepts are meant to be read before the reference.

nodes.label: Java Docs Page
nodes.rationale: Embeds the full generated Javadoc for all modules in an iframe with a toolbar linking the package index and all-classes index.

nodes.label: Failover Library
nodes.rationale: Open-source Spring Boot library built at Societe Generale for transparent failover of referential data; licensed Apache 2.0.

nodes.label: Referential Outage Cascade
nodes.rationale: Dozens of services depend on the same small set of slow-changing but constantly-queried referential systems (currency tables, country lists, client profiles), so one referential outage becomes a full-platform incident. Rather than solve it N times with bespoke try/catch, the team built one reusable annotation-driven solution (ADR 1).

nodes.label: Design Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Four principles: minimal integration (one annotation, no framework coupling); business-driven expiry (TTL is a business decision the framework enforces and teams configure); observable by default (structured logs and Micrometer metrics with no extra instrumentation); pluggable at every seam (store, key generation, expiry policy, payload enrichment, exception policy, context propagation all replaceable without modifying the framework).

nodes.label: Anand Manissery
nodes.rationale: Creator and lead maintainer. Other acknowledged contributors: Vincent Fuchs (contributions and review), Patrice Fricard, Igor Lovich, Abilash Titus (early contributors).

nodes.label: Contribution Workflow
nodes.rationale: Fork, branch, keep scope to one feature or fix per PR, add or update tests for every behaviour change, run mvn verify with zero Javadoc warnings, then open a PR against main. Prerequisites: JDK 21+, Maven 3.9+, Git. PRs with no activity for 30 days may be closed.

nodes.label: Coding Conventions
nodes.rationale: Java 21 with Spring Boot 4.x idioms; every public type and method needs Javadoc; no breaking public-API changes without a deprecation cycle and a new ADR.

nodes.label: ADR Process for Architecture Decisions
nodes.rationale: New architecture decisions are appended as a new ADR; large changes should start as a discussion or ADR before any code is written.

nodes.label: Failover Interception Model
nodes.rationale: On success the result is serialised to the store; on any exception the last stored result for the same arguments is returned so the caller sees stale-but-valid data instead of an error. If nothing is stored the exception is re-thrown (default) or null returned per exception policy.

nodes.label: Spring Proxy Requirement
nodes.rationale: Works with any Spring-container-managed AOP-proxied bean (Feign clients, @Service, @Component, @Repository, Spring Data repositories, @RestController) but the method must be invoked through the proxy, not via this.method() inside the same class. Plain Java objects are invisible to both the aspect and the scanner.

nodes.label: Optional Referential / ReferentialAware Model
nodes.rationale: No domain-model change is required; extending Referential or implementing ReferentialAware is optional and only adds upToDate, asOf and metadata so callers can distinguish live from stale data.

nodes.label: Store Choice in Production
nodes.rationale: Use JDBC in production: it persists across restarts, works across multiple instances, and is the only store supporting schema-level multi-tenancy. INMEMORY and CAFFEINE lose data on restart and belong in local development or tests.

nodes.label: Exception Policy (RETHROW / NEVER_THROW / custom)
nodes.rationale: RETHROW (default) re-throws the original exception on store miss; NEVER_THROW returns null or the RecoveredPayloadHandler result. All Throwables trigger recovery with no type filtering; narrowing that requires a custom FailoverExecution or the RESILIENCE type with a Resilience4j predicate.

nodes.label: MethodExceptionPolicy
nodes.rationale: Registered with failover.exception-policy: custom to wrap or translate the exception thrown on total failure, receiving a MethodExceptionContext carrying recoveredResult() and cause().

nodes.label: RecoveredPayloadHandler
nodes.rationale: Returns a default or sentinel value instead of null on store miss; can also be used to increment a recovery counter for monitoring.

nodes.label: Jackson Payload Serialisation
nodes.rationale: Payloads are JSON via Jackson with PAYLOAD_CLASS holding the FQCN for deserialisation, so domain types need a public no-arg constructor or @JsonCreator, readable fields, and no unresolvable type references. Renamed or removed fields break recovery of already-stored rows.

nodes.label: PayloadColumnResolver
nodes.rationale: For payloads exceeding VARCHAR(4000): either change the DDL to TEXT/CLOB or implement PayloadColumnResolver returning Types.CLOB from payloadType() and reading via getClob().

nodes.label: FAILOVER_STORE Table
nodes.rationale: Columns FAILOVER_NAME, FAILOVER_KEY, AS_OF, EXPIRE_ON, PAYLOAD, PAYLOAD_CLASS with primary key (FAILOVER_NAME, FAILOVER_KEY); the table name carries the failover.store.jdbc.table-prefix. The compound primary key is what makes concurrent multi-instance upserts safe.

nodes.label: Store Key Derivation
nodes.rationale: The default KeyGenerator joins all method arguments' toString() and MD5-hashes them into a fixed-length UUID-based key; the compound lookup is (name, key). Adding an argument silently changes the key so old entries stop matching — a custom KeyGenerator excluding it preserves backward compatibility. Different names never share entries regardless of argument overlap.

nodes.label: ExpiryCleanupScheduler
nodes.rationale: Runs on failover.scheduler.cleanup-cron (hourly by default) deleting rows where EXPIRE_ON < now, so the store does not grow without bound. Disable only when cleanup is managed externally, e.g. to batch deletes with a cursor and avoid lock contention.

nodes.label: Expired Entry Semantics
nodes.rationale: An expired entry is treated exactly like a missing one — it is never returned even if the row physically exists; the framework returns null or re-throws per the exception policy.

nodes.label: Async Store Write Trade-offs
nodes.rationale: Every success pays serialisation plus an insert/upsert; async offloads it so the caller is not blocked, and a store failure on the write path is logged without propagating. The costs: writes can be dropped when the test context shuts down first, and there is no exactly-once guarantee — concurrent writes for the same (name, key) race and the native upsert resolves last-write-wins with no distributed lock, which is acceptable for idempotent referential data.

nodes.label: TABLE_PREFIX vs SCHEMA Multi-tenancy
nodes.rationale: TABLE_PREFIX gives each tenant its own table via failover.store.multitenant.tenants. SCHEMA gives each tenant its own schema through a TenantStoreFactory bean and requires failover.store.async=false, because thread-local schema switching (e.g. SET search_path) is not carried by background async threads — otherwise connection leaks and wrong-schema errors appear.

nodes.label: DatabaseResolver and Silent Fallback
nodes.rationale: DefaultDatabaseResolver reads the product name from JDBC metadata; if metadata access is restricted or the name is unexpected, resolve() returns null, the merge query is disabled, and the store silently uses INSERT + UPDATE. A hardcoded DatabaseResolver bean forces the correct dialect.

nodes.label: PayloadSplitter Partial Recovery
nodes.rationale: Use it when a method returns a collection but entries should be stored per element, so if three of five items are stored those three are still returned with the upstream fully down. Each scatter slot dispatches on its own virtual thread, so thread-local security/tenant/trace context needs a ContextPropagator.

nodes.label: ObservablePublisher
nodes.rationale: Implemented to receive failover metrics and forward them to Micrometer, Prometheus, Datadog or another backend.

nodes.label: GraalVM Native Image Support
nodes.rationale: Not officially tested; Jackson serialisation and Spring AOP proxy generation are the concerns. Boot's native support handles AOP proxies but reflection-based domain deserialisation may need explicit Jackson type hints.

nodes.label: Recovery Troubleshooting Checklist
nodes.rationale: When recovery unexpectedly misses: key mismatch between store and recover arguments, expired EXPIRE_ON, wrong @Failover name, or an async write race. Enable DEBUG on com.societegenerale.failover to log the generated key on every store and recover call, and set failover.store.async=false in tests.

nodes.label: Duplicate Failover Name Startup Failure
nodes.rationale: Two annotations sharing a name would collide in the store and overwrite each other's entries on recovery, so startup fails with a duplicate-name error to prevent it.

nodes.label: Prefer a Real Store in Behaviour Tests
nodes.rationale: Mock the store only when testing an SPI implementation in isolation; for end-to-end failover behaviour use the real JDBC store on H2, because mocking skips serialisation, key derivation, expiry and enrichment — where most integration issues actually occur.
nodes.norm_label: prefer a real store in behaviour tests

nodes.label: Support Channels
nodes.rationale: GitHub Issues for bugs (bug label) and feature requests (enhancement label, describing the use case not just the solution); GitHub Discussions for how-do-I questions and architectural advice — question issues are converted to discussions. Best-effort response times; PRs with tests land fastest.

nodes.label: Security Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Never open a public issue; use GitHub private vulnerability reporting or email the maintainers per SECURITY.md.

nodes.label: main.html MkDocs Template Override
nodes.rationale: Extends the Material base.html and overrides the content block to inject a styled page banner before super().

nodes.label: fo-page-banner
nodes.rationale: Rendered on every non-home content page with a title: a decorative faded watermark icon plus an inline icon from page.meta.icon, the parent section title (or site_name) as an eyebrow, and the page title as h1. Suppressed on the home page, detected by 'navigation' being in page.meta.hide.

nodes.label: 24-Community Bridge Is an Extraction Artifact
nodes.rationale: The apparent bridging of 24 communities by core_defaultfailoverstore (type=concept, source=docs/adr/adr.md, degree=108) is not real architecture — it is a fuzzy-dedup collapse of at least three distinct classes into one node.

nodes.label: Fuzzy Dedup Collapse
nodes.rationale: The merge step reported 908 deduplicated nodes, 404 of them fuzzy; core_defaultfailoverstore is one of them, absorbing the store class, the JDBC query resolver, and DefaultFailoverHandler's method surface plus a false 'implements FailoverHandler' edge.

nodes.label: DefaultFailoverStore
nodes.rationale: Implements FailoverStore and FailoverStoreSizeAware with exactly seven methods: store, delete, find, findAll, cleanByExpiry, liveEntryCount, liveEntryCountSupported. It does NOT implement FailoverHandler.

nodes.label: DefaultFailoverStoreQueryResolver (Absorbed Node)
nodes.rationale: Owns validateTablePrefix, resolveMergeQuery, applyPrefix, buildInsertMergeTypes, buildUpdateTypes, DatabaseResolver and PayloadColumnResolver, yet has zero nodes of its own in the graph — it was entirely absorbed into core_defaultfailoverstore.

nodes.label: DefaultFailoverHandler (Split Across 3 Nodes)
nodes.rationale: Its recover, recoverAll, doRecover and clean surface was partly absorbed into core_defaultfailoverstore, while the class itself resolves to three separate nodes — the inverse of the collapse defect.

nodes.label: FailoverStoreJdbc (Split Across 5 Nodes)
nodes.rationale: Resolves to five separate graph nodes under inconsistent ID schemes; AdvancedFailoverHandler likewise resolves to three.

nodes.label: Inconsistent Node ID Scheme
nodes.rationale: Duplicate class nodes carry inconsistent IDs including at least one full-path ID that violates the parent_dir_filename_entity rule, which is what lets the same class split into several nodes.

nodes.label: God-node Degree and Betweenness Distortion
nodes.rationale: Because collapse inflates degree and splitting deflates it, god-node rankings and betweenness-derived questions in GRAPH_REPORT.md partly measure dedup damage rather than real coupling. Remedy: graphify extract --force to rebuild IDs cleanly.
